name: Wu Caiping
current_role: Individual top-10 shareholder (~2.6%) of Guangzhou Shiyuan Electronic Technology (CVTE, SZSE: 002841)
profile: Wu Caiping (吴彩平) is a long-standing individual shareholder of CVTE (Shiyuan Electronic), the Guangzhou maker of interactive flat panels, display control boards and the Seewo/MAXHUB brands, listed in Shenzhen in 2017. Wealth comes from that stake (~18.3m shares, ~2.6% as of Sept 2026). Not part of the founders' concerted-action group and holds no disclosed executive role; otherwise very low profile.
interesting_fact: Ranked among CVTE's top 10 shareholders in the 2024 annual report alongside founders Huang Zhengcong, Wang Yiran and Sun Yonghui; CVTE, founded in 2005, is one of the world's largest suppliers of LCD TV main control boards and interactive whiteboards.
notes: Very private passive shareholder; no public interviews found. Only route is CVTE's board-secretary/IR office (email is company IR, not personal). Gender and age not confirmed.

name: Ye Dalin
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Zhejiang Tailin Bioengineering Co., Ltd. (SZSE ChiNext: 300813)
profile: Ye Dalin (叶大林, b. 1960) founded Hangzhou-based Tailin Bioengineering, which makes sterility-testing, microbial-detection, filtration and isolator equipment for pharma and biotech labs. He and his wife Ni Weiju are the controlling shareholders (~57%), and the company listed on ChiNext in 2020. In 2026 Tailin was pursuing a convertible-bond issue to fund high-performance filter and functional-membrane production.
interesting_fact: Tailin's core products are sterility-test pumps and microbial-limit testers used by drug makers, and its 2026 fundraising targets industrialising high-performance filters and functional membranes.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming an entrepreneur he spent 13 years as a lab technician: at Zhejiang Hospital (1981-88) and the Hangzhou Central Blood Station (1988-94), then ran the Zhejiang Pan'an Kaixuan microporous filter factory (1994-99) before founding Hangzhou Tailin Industrial in 1999.
notes: Low media profile; best route is the company board-secretary office. Wealth shared with wife Ni Weiju.

name: Wang Yaofang
current_role: Chairman and Party Secretary, Changzhou Qianhong Bio-Pharma (SZSE: 002550); controlling shareholder (~20%)
profile: Wang Yaofang (王耀方, b. 1953), a senior engineer and licensed pharmacist, rose from deputy director of the state-owned Changzhou Biochemical Pharmaceutical Factory to lead its restructured successor, Qianhong Bio-Pharma, a heparin API and enzyme-drug maker he took public in Shenzhen in 2011. Qianhong is now pushing original drugs such as QHRD106 and QHRD107 through clinical trials.
interesting_fact: Qianhong is one of China's main exporters of heparin sodium API (made from pig intestinal mucosa) and also sells pancreatic kininogenase; at a May 2026 earnings call Wang said its novel drugs QHRD106 (Phase IIb) and QHRD107 (Phase IIa) were on schedule.
deep_cut_fact: He began at the state-run Changzhou Biochemical Pharmaceutical Factory, rising to deputy factory director, before leading its spin-out Changzhou Biochemical Qianhong Pharmaceutical as chairman and GM; he holds three professional titles: senior engineer, national licensed pharmacist and senior economist.
notes: Since the 2024 annual report the company's legal representative is Wang Ke (acts in concert with Wang Yaofang); confirm current chairman title before outreach. Best route: board secretary office.

name: Hugh Osmond
current_role: Founder, Sun Capital Partners (2001) and Osmond Capital (2017); Non-Executive Director, Coppa Collective plc (formerly Various Eateries, AIM)
profile: Hugh Osmond (b. 1962), an Oxford-educated former medic, co-led the 1993 PizzaExpress flotation with Luke Johnson, founded pub group Punch Taverns in 1997 and co-founded closed-life-fund consolidator Pearl Group (bought from Henderson for GBP1.1bn in 2005). He now invests via Sun Capital and Osmond Capital, bought Capital Physio in 2019, and founded Coppa Club operator Various Eateries in 2014.
interesting_fact: Read medicine at Merton College, Oxford, but went into hospitality; he spotted in early-1990s America how many places served a decent meal for $5-10, which convinced him and Luke Johnson that PizzaExpress could become a national chain.
deep_cut_fact: He started running clubs and bars while at university, ran clubs in America after graduating in 1983, and admits to a brief stint trying to run a computer company ('I don't know what possessed me') before working at a small Madrid investment bank.

public_contacts.value: Alma PR (Coppa Collective's PR adviser), 71-73 Carter Lane, London EC4V 5EQ

notes: Significant Conservative Party donor. No personal social accounts found; best route is via Coppa Collective's PR (Alma PR) or Osmond Capital.

name: Wang Jianhua
current_role: Director and Chief Technology Officer, Qingdao Topscomm Communication Inc. (SSE: 603421); chairman 2012-May 2025
profile: Wang Jianhua (王建华, b. 1966), a senior engineer with a postgraduate degree, co-founded Qingdao Topscomm with Zeng Fanyi in 2008. Topscomm makes power-line carrier communication chips and modules, smart-meter and grid-automation equipment sold largely to China's State Grid, and listed in Shanghai in 2016. He chaired the company until May 2025 (succeeded by Liu Min) and remains a director, CTO and a major shareholder (~91.6m shares).
interesting_fact: Topscomm is a grid-edge tech play: it designs its own power-line carrier (PLC) communication chips used in electricity-meter reading networks, and its business scope now spans energy storage, EV charging and PV equipment.
deep_cut_fact: Unusually for a founder-chairman, he doubled as the company's hands-on technologist: CTO since 2015 and, from 2019 to 2024, head of Topscomm's in-house Chip and Basic Theory Research Institute; he also runs its fire-safety subsidiary Dingxin Xiaofang.
notes: Strong fit for an energy/grid-tech episode (PLC chips for smart grid). Low media profile; route via Topscomm securities office.

name: Sharon Harel
current_role: Founder, WestEnd Films (London film/TV production, financing and international sales company)
profile: Sharon Harel-Cohen is a London-based film producer and financier who has produced or financed 50+ films, chiefly through Capitol Films, which she co-founded in 1989 and sold in 2006 (Gosford Park, Spider, Death and the Maiden). In 2008 she launched WestEnd Films with Eve Schoukroun and Maya Amsellem; its credits include HBO's Valley of Tears. Her listed wealth is shared with her husband, private-equity and impact-investing pioneer Sir Ronald Cohen.
interesting_fact: Executive producer on Robert Altman's Gosford Park, Polanski's Death and the Maiden and the Oscar-nominated Albert Nobbs; she received the Olswang Business Award from Carlton Women in Film and Television in 2002.
deep_cut_fact: She began as a producer in Israel on the classic Halahaka ('The Troupe'), which she co-wrote, then produced Tom Hanks' 1986 Tri-Star film Every Time We Say Goodbye; her degree from the Hebrew University of Jerusalem is in Chinese Studies and Western Philosophy.
notes: Also known as Sharon Harel-Cohen / Lady Cohen. Best route is WestEnd Films general inbox. Husband Sir Ronald Cohen (Apax founder, impact investing) may be the more relevant podcast guest.

name: Charles W Scharf
current_role: Chairman (since Oct 2025) and CEO (since Oct 2019), Wells Fargo & Company; Director, Microsoft
profile: Charlie Scharf (b. 1965) is a career banker who rose under Jamie Dimon from Commercial Credit through Salomon Smith Barney, Citigroup, Bank One and JPMorgan Chase, where he ran retail and integrated Washington Mutual in 2008. He was CEO of Visa (2012-16) and BNY Mellon (2017-19) before taking over Wells Fargo in 2019 to work through its regulatory consent orders; he became chairman in 2025 and sits on Microsoft's board.
interesting_fact: Jamie Dimon hired him in 1987 for a back-office job at Commercial Credit; within six months he was Dimon's assistant, and he spent some 25 years working alongside Dimon before becoming a rival bank CEO.
deep_cut_fact: Son of a stockbroker, he grew up in Westfield, New Jersey, and as a teenager worked back-office jobs at Manhattan brokerage firms; he earned his NYU Stern MBA at night (executive programme, 1991) while already working for Dimon.
notes: Highly visible Fortune-100 CEO; requests go via Wells Fargo corporate communications (newsroom.wf.com). Microsoft board seat is relevant to a data-center angle.

name: Arun K Chittilappilly
current_role: Managing Director, Wonderla Holidays Ltd (India's largest amusement-park chain); promoter shareholder of V-Guard Industries
profile: Arun K. Chittilappilly is the elder son of V-Guard founder Kochouseph Chittilappilly and a promoter-shareholder of V-Guard Industries, the Kerala-based maker of voltage stabilisers, inverters, wires and appliances. He co-promoted and runs listed Wonderla Holidays, which grew from the Veegaland water park in Kochi (2000) to parks in Bengaluru (2005), Hyderabad (2016), Bhubaneswar (2024) and Chennai (2025).
interesting_fact: Wonderla started as 'Veegaland' in Kochi in 2000; Arun and his father then built the 82-acre Wonderla Bengaluru for about INR105 crore in 2005, and the Kochi park was rebranded Wonderla in 2011.
deep_cut_fact: In January 2018 he personally launched 'Recoil', a reverse-looping roller coaster that is Wonderla Hyderabad's signature ride, alongside CEO D.S. Sachdeva.
notes: Hurun lists his wealth under V-Guard (family holding); his operating role is at Wonderla. Confirm he is still MD before outreach (search budget ran out in this pass).

name: Mark H Md Rachesky
current_role: Founder and President, MHR Fund Management (NYC); Chairman, Lionsgate Studios; director and 10% owner, Starz Entertainment
profile: Mark Rachesky, M.D. (b. 1960) founded MHR Fund Management in 1996, a New York special-situations investor managing 5bn+ dollars across distressed debt, equity, capital solutions, litigation finance and life settlements. MHR's best-known bet is its controlling stake in Lions Gate, which he chairs; after the 2025 Lionsgate/Starz separation he sits on both boards. MHR has also invested in trucking and energy companies.
interesting_fact: He holds an M.D. and an MBA from Stanford (plus a biology B.S. from Penn), hence the 'Md' in his SEC filer name - a rare physician turned distressed-debt investor and Hollywood studio chairman.
deep_cut_fact: Forbes (2013) profiled him as 'The Smart Money Behind The Hunger Games', noting he built MHR by taking control of companies like Lions Gate cheaply via their debt; his family foundation supports UJA-Federation, the Museum of Jewish Heritage and Penn.
notes: Low public profile, rarely gives interviews. Only published firm contact is MHR's IR inbox (investor-focused); Lionsgate corporate communications is an alternative route. MHR's energy holdings may be a podcast angle.

name: Earl Spencer
current_role: 9th Earl Spencer; owner of the Althorp estate (Northamptonshire); historian, author, broadcaster and podcast co-host
profile: Charles Spencer, 9th Earl Spencer (b. 1964), younger brother of Diana, Princess of Wales, inherited the earldom and Althorp in 1992; the family's land and art collection date back to Tudor-era sheep-farming wealth. A former NBC News correspondent, he is now a bestselling popular historian (Killers of the King, To Catch a King), runs Althorp and co-hosts the podcast The Rabbit Hole Detectives.
interesting_fact: Before inheriting, he was an on-air correspondent for NBC's Today show and Nightly News (1986-95) and wrote/presented the 12-part series Great Houses of the World; since 2009 he has re-roofed Althorp and restored its entire exterior for the first time since the 1780s.
deep_cut_fact: He founded the Althorp Literary Festival in 2003 (speakers have included Bill Bryson and Antonia Fraser) and in 2021 wrote an audio walking tour of St James's Park, 'Death of a King: The Path to Execution', tracing Charles I's final walk, for the BARDEUM app.

public_contacts.value: The Rabbit Hole Detectives (with Richard Coles and Cat Jarman)

notes: Media-savvy and podcast-experienced, but his 2026 Diana memoir 'Swan Song' generated heavy controversy - avoid royal topics; history, Althorp estate stewardship or land/energy use are safer angles. Did not verify his personal social accounts.

name: John A. Bartholdson
current_role: Co-founder and Partner, Juniper Investment Company (NYC); Non-Executive Chair, Lincoln Educational Services (Lincoln Tech); Director, Bioventus
profile: John Bartholdson (age 55) co-founded Juniper Investment Company in 2007 with Alexis Michas; it takes concentrated stakes in public and private companies. He chairs career-training school operator Lincoln Tech (board since a 2019 Series A preferred deal), chairs private device maker Theragenics, and sits on Bioventus' board. He was earlier a partner at Stonington Partners (1997-2011).
interesting_fact: As chair of Lincoln Tech he oversees one of the largest US trade-school networks training electricians, HVAC and automotive technicians - the skilled-trades pipeline that data-center and energy build-outs depend on.
deep_cut_fact: He began as an analyst at Merrill Lynch Capital Partners (1992-94) after Duke, then took a Stanford MBA; he previously sat on the board of skincare company Obagi Medical Products until its 2013 sale to Valeant.
notes: SEC-derived net worth likely overstates personal wealth: much of it is Juniper fund holdings in which he disclaims beneficial ownership beyond his pecuniary interest. No published direct contact found; Juniper's office is at 555 Madison Ave, New York (per proxy). Route via Lincoln Tech or Bioventus corporate secretary.

name: Todd Foley
current_role: Managing Director, MPM BioImpact; co-founder and Board Chair, Aktis Oncology (Nasdaq: AKTS)
profile: Todd Foley has been a biotech venture investor at MPM Capital (now MPM BioImpact) since 1999. He co-founded radiopharmaceutical developer Aktis Oncology, chairing it since 2020 through its January 2026 IPO, and has served on the boards of Rhythm Pharmaceuticals, Repare Therapeutics, Entrada Therapeutics and Chiasma. His SEC-reported holdings largely reflect MPM fund stakes.
interesting_fact: Aktis Oncology, which he co-founded and chairs, is developing targeted radiopharmaceuticals (radioactive-isotope cancer drugs) aimed at large tumour populations not reached by existing platforms; it listed on Nasdaq in January 2026.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a chemist - a BS in Chemistry from MIT - before his Harvard MBA, and has spent his entire 25+ year investing career at one firm, MPM, which he joined in 1999.
notes: Holdings are mostly via MPM funds, so personal net worth is likely overstated. MPM BioImpact website blocked automated access; its contact page is the likely route. Isotope supply-chain angle could tie into energy/nuclear topics.

name: Ruben Kliksberg
current_role: Managing Member of Double Twins K, LLC, the general partner controlling Redwood Capital Management (New York credit/special-situations manager)
profile: Ruben Kliksberg controls Redwood Capital Management, a New York and Sunny Isles Beach, Florida alternative investment manager founded in 2000 that focuses on opportunistic credit and special situations. Through the Redwood funds he reported a ~19.7% stake (4.3m shares) in Office Properties Income Trust in a June 2026 Schedule 13D, making him a 10% owner; Redwood has filed on OPI since 2022.
interesting_fact: Redwood's OPI position gives it, per its own 13D, 'significant influence' over the REIT's strategy and board elections - a credit fund ending up as a top owner of a portfolio of US office buildings.
notes: Very low public profile; SEC net-worth figure reflects Redwood fund holdings he is deemed to beneficially own, not necessarily personal wealth. Personal biography not verified (search budget exhausted in this pass); route via Redwood's general inbox.

name: Prashant Bangur
current_role: Vice Chairman, Shree Cement Ltd (per company website)
profile: Prashant Bangur is a member of the Kolkata-based Bangur family that controls Shree Cement, one of India's largest cement makers, headquartered in Rajasthan. He holds a maths degree from St. Xavier's Kolkata and an ISB MBA in finance and logistics, served as whole-time director and is now vice chairman, and sits on the national management committee of the Cement Manufacturers' Association.
interesting_fact: Shree Cement doubles as a power producer: it commissioned a 300 MW thermal power plant at Beawar, Rajasthan in 2012 and moved into selling electricity.
deep_cut_fact: In 2011 the World Economic Forum named him a 'New Sustainability Champion' - Shree says it was the only cement company nominated - for its push to be the greenest cement maker.
notes: Strong energy angle (captive power, power sales). Confirm current title before outreach - board roles were reshuffled in recent years and could not be re-checked (search budget exhausted).

name: Bharat Kanaiyalal Sheth
current_role: Chairman and Managing Director (since Nov 2025), The Great Eastern Shipping Co. Ltd; Chairman, Greatship (India) Ltd
profile: Bharat K. Sheth (b. 1958) has spent his whole career at Great Eastern Shipping, India's largest private-sector shipping company (tankers, gas carriers and dry bulk), founded by his family in 1948. He joined in 1981, became executive director in 1989, MD in 1999, deputy chairman and MD in 2005 and chairman and MD in November 2025. He also chairs offshore-services arm Greatship (India).
interesting_fact: Great Eastern's fleet hauls crude, products and LPG - making it a bellwether for India's energy imports - and the group also runs Greatship (India), an offshore oilfield services company.
deep_cut_fact: He studied economics (honours) at the University of St Andrews in Scotland, and cut his teeth at the company in chartering and ship sale-and-purchase - the part of the business the company's own bio calls 'the most intricate' in shipping.
notes: Company holds regular analyst calls and he speaks publicly on shipping markets; corporate communications is the best route. Energy-shipping angle fits the podcast.
